title: How much protein is really in an egg?

seo.title: How much protein is really in an egg?
seo.meta_description: A large egg contains about 6.3 g of protein. The white supplies roughly 3.6 g and the yolk around 2.7 g; size changes the total.
seo.search_intent: Find the actual protein in one egg and understand how size, white and yolk affect it.

excerpt: A U.S. large egg, about 50 g edible weight, contains roughly 6.3 g of protein. The white contributes about 3.6 g and the yolk about 2.7 g. Smaller eggs provide less and extra-large eggs more, so 'one egg' is not a perfectly fixed unit.
content_html:
A large egg is a convenient nutrition unit, but eggs come in different sizes. The familiar “6 grams of protein per egg” is therefore a useful shorthand, not a universal constant.

USDA data put a large egg at about 50 g edible weight and roughly 6.3 g protein.

AmountProtein
1 large whole egg~6.3 g
Large egg white~3.6 g
Large yolk~2.7 g
2 large eggs~12.6 g
3 large eggs~19 g

The yolk contains protein too

The white supplies slightly more than half of the egg's protein, but the yolk is not just fat. Removing it also removes around 2.5–3 g protein per large egg along with nutrients such as choline, vitamin B12 and vitamin D.

Size changes the total

Small eggs may be closer to 5 g protein, while extra-large and jumbo eggs can approach 7–8 g. If a recipe or nutrition target depends on precision, “large egg” is a better unit than simply “egg.”

Cooking changes structure, not the basic amount

Heat denatures egg proteins and makes cooked egg easier to digest, but it does not create additional protein. Small changes in protein per 100 g mostly reflect changes in water and final weight.

The practical number

Use about 6.3 g per large egg for everyday calculations. Two eggs supply about 12–13 g; three bring the meal close to 19 g.

faq.question: How much protein is in two eggs?
faq.answer: Two U.S. large eggs provide about 12.6 g of protein.

faq.question: Does the egg white contain all the protein?
faq.answer: No. A large white has about 3.6 g while the yolk contributes roughly 2.7 g.
